## Intent
Hypothesis: a branchless per-particle blend with hash-based RNG and identity ordering can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling by eliminating branch divergence while preserving sequential access.

## Cache saturation
Working set is 68·N bytes; L1d spills at N≈963, L2 at N≈61680. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 10.333 ns/p (N=4000, just past L1d) to 6.074 ns/p (N=16000) as per-particle overhead amortizes. Across the L2→DRAM spill (N≈61680, between N=16000 and N=65000), cost stays FLAT—6.074→5.904 ns/p, no knee. A minimum of 5.862 ns/p occurs at N=262000, then cost RISES slightly to 6.154 ns/p at N=4000000. The absence of a spill knee indicates hash-RNG compute density masks DRAM latency. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.25 holds ~8.4 ns/p from N=16000 onward—same amortization-then-flat profile, ~40% higher.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 11.6 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 = 46% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.05, peak is 10.89 GB/s (43%); at q=0.25, 8.26 GB/s (33%). The algo is overhead-bound at small N (6.58 GB/s at N=4000) and reaches a compute-bound plateau by N=16000 where bandwidth stabilizes regardless of N growth. It never approaches the streaming ceiling: the hash-RNG integer chains (eor/mul/lsr) and the byte-granular scatter in the render phase consume cycles that could otherwise stream. Death rate is the dominant depressor—each 5× increase in q costs ~2 GB/s.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. The update loop uses `fmul.4s v18, v21, v2` and `fadd.4s v18, v19, v18` on 4-lane vectors assembled via `ext.16b v21, v19, v20, #0xc` and `mov.s v21[3], v18[0]`—rearranging particle fields into contiguous lanes. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v20}[1], [x24]` loads one element into a lane. Constants are broadcast with `dup.4s v2, w16` and `dup.2s v0, w16`; stores are wide (`stur q18`, `stur d18`). Yet only 9 of 319 instructions are vector-suffixed; the bulk is scalar integer hash computation (eor=9, mul=7, lsr=4) and scalar FP (fadd=11, fmul=10). The render phase is entirely scalar: 17 `strb` byte stores with `ldrb`/`csel` clamping, which cannot stream and cap bandwidth below ceiling.

## Verdict
Partially holds—the branchless blend shows no cache-spill knee (6.074→5.904 ns/p across the L2→DRAM transition at N≈61680), confirming streaming-like access from identity ordering. But the hypothesis of approaching the streaming ceiling is refuted: peak is 11.6 GB/s = 46% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling at q=0.01, N=262000, limited by hash-RNG compute density and 17 byte-granular `strb` scatter stores. At q=0.25, bandwidth falls to 8.04 GB/s (32%), so the branchless advantage erodes under churn.
